title: API gateway: tune fallback timeouts + retry budgets during regional failover; add Retry-After overload responses
author: Peter Holtz
release_notes:
- During regional impairments/failover, the gateway enforces a smaller retry budget and tighter per-hop timeouts to reduce thundering herd.
- Standardizes explicit overload responses with Retry-After for upstream exhaustion (helps clients back off cleanly).
- Adds metrics for overload responses + retry budget exhaustion to support failover dashboards.
content:
Title: API gateway: tune fallback timeouts + retry budgets during regional failover; add Retry-After overload responses

Context
During failover drills and a couple of real partial impairments, we saw gateway retries + long tail timeouts amplify load. When a region is impaired (or when routing is actively moving traffic), the existing retry budgets can cause: (1) request fan-out across regions (client retries + gateway retries), (2) work amplification against already-constrained capacity, (3) noisy error/latency signals that delay decisive failover.

This PR tightens timeouts/retry behavior when failover is active or when the upstream is overloaded, and introduces explicit Retry-After responses for overload so clients can apply deterministic backoff.

What changed (high level)
- Retry budget policy:
  - Introduce a “failover mode” retry budget profile that is automatically enabled when routing marks a route/region as degraded OR when the gateway observes consecutive upstream overload signals.
  - In failover mode we reduce max retries and cap total retry time (wall clock) per request.
- Timeout tuning:
  - Reduce upstream connect + response header timeouts in failover mode (we prefer fast failure + reroute over slow hangs).
  - Ensure streaming requests fail quickly on cross-region redirect paths so the client can reconnect (ties to ENG-2422 follow-up).
- Explicit overload response:
  - When upstream returns/indicates overload (or circuit breaker opens), gateway responds with 429 (or 503 where semantically required) and sets Retry-After with a bounded jittered value.
  - Adds an internal header to preserve reason codes for debugging while avoiding leaking internal topology.
- Circuit breaker integration:
  - Treat circuit-breaker open as authoritative overload for retry policy evaluation.
  - Do not retry non-idempotent requests unless the request is explicitly marked idempotent by the client (existing behavior preserved; now stricter under failover mode).

Behavior details
- Overload response mapping:
  - If upstream is saturated or CB is open: respond 429 Too Many Requests (Hosted API) with `Retry-After: <seconds>`.
  - If endpoint requires 503 by contract (some internal control-plane paths): respond 503 Service Unavailable with `Retry-After`.
  - Streaming: if redirect/failover triggers mid-stream, return a terminal frame that includes an error code and Retry-After guidance; clients should reconnect (see notes below).

- Retry budget:
  - Normal mode defaults unchanged.
  - Failover mode:
    - max_attempts: 2 (1 initial + 1 retry)
    - max_total_retry_time: 800ms (non-streaming) / 1200ms (streaming handshake)
    - backoff: exponential with decorrelated jitter, capped at 250ms

Why this is safe
- Changes are gated behind a feature flag: `gateway.failover_tuned_retry_budget` (default OFF in prod; ON in staging).
- Retry-After is only emitted for overload/circuit-breaker conditions (not for generic 5xx).
- We preserve idempotency rules and further restrict retries under failover mode.

Observability
New metrics (names are illustrative; see files below for exact names):
- `gateway_overload_responses_total{route,tier,reason}`
- `gateway_retry_budget_exhausted_total{route,tier,mode}`
- `gateway_upstream_timeout_total{route,tier,mode}`
Also adds log annotations when failover mode is entered/exited for a route.

Files / areas changed
- api-gateway
  - retry_budget.go: add failover profile + gating logic
  - timeouts.go: per-mode upstream timeouts + defaults
  - overload_response.go: 429/503 mapping + Retry-After
  - streaming/termination.go: terminal frame mapping for overload
- config
  - gateway feature flag config + safe defaults
- docs (internal)
  - runbook snippet: how to recognize Retry-After overload vs regional impairment

Illustrative snippet
- Example overload response headers:
  - `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests`
  - `Retry-After: 2`
  - `x-redwood-overload: 1` (internal-only in logs; not forwarded to clients)

Testing
- Unit tests:
  - retry budget switches to failover mode when routing marks region degraded
  - retry budget switches to failover mode when CB open trips
  - Retry-After header present and within bounds (1–5s with jitter)
  - Non-idempotent requests not retried under failover mode
- Integration tests (staging):
  - Simulated overload returns 429 + Retry-After and reduces repeat request rate
  - Cross-region redirect path does not exceed max_total_retry_time

Rollout plan
1) Enable in staging for all tenants + validate metrics / no regression (24h).
2) Enable in prod for canary routes only (Hosted: /v1/chat, /v1/completions; Dedicated: selected pools).
3) Expand to all routes once burn-rate alerts show reduced oscillation and we confirm no client compatibility issues.

Notes / follow-ups
- Client-facing guidance will be updated in the SDK docs to respect Retry-After (tracked separately; see redwood-docs PR).
- Streaming reconnect improvements are in progress (ENG-2422 / PR-19821).

Checklist
- [x] Feature-flagged and default OFF in prod
- [x] Unit tests added
- [x] Added metrics + dashboard hooks
- [x] Verified no PII in overload reason logs
- [x] SRE sign-off for game day readiness

Commits
1) gateway: add failover-mode retry budget profile
2) gateway: tune upstream timeouts for failover mode
3) gateway: implement overload responses with Retry-After
4) gateway: add metrics + log annotations
5) tests: cover retry/timeout/overload behavior

Review conversation (highlights)
- Miles Thornton: “We need to be very explicit about when failover mode activates. Please ensure it’s not driven by a single noisy 5xx signal.”
  - Peter Holtz (author): “Agreed. Activation is based on routing ‘degraded’ OR circuit-breaker open OR sustained overload counter for N=20 requests in 30s; not generic 5xx burn. Added test + docs in code comments.”

- Mina Haddad: “Can we guarantee we don’t flip-flop between normal/failover budgets?”
  - Peter: “Added hold-down timer of 2 minutes after entering failover mode; exit requires 5 minutes healthy + CB closed. (Matches general anti-flap guidance; aligns with ongoing ADR work.)”

- Allison Grant: “Metric label cardinality: please don’t include tenant_id or model in the new overload metrics.”
  - Peter: “Confirmed: route + tier + coarse reason only. No tenant/model labels. Added comment + lint check for disallowed labels.”

- Tomáš Novák: “Please add a runbook note so on-call knows Retry-After spikes are expected during protective shedding and not necessarily a routing bug.”
  - Peter: “Added internal runbook snippet + log annotation pointers.”

CI
- Build: pass
- Unit tests: pass
- Lint: pass
- One initial failure due to flaky integration test timing; reran after tightening deterministic clock in the test harness.

Merge outcome
Merged (squash) into main on 2026-01-13.

Related
- Linear: ENG-2419 (Update API gateway circuit breakers), ENG-2411 (Umbrella)
- Jira: SUP-25310 (Transient 5xx during planned routing test), SUP-25322 (Streaming disconnects during region redirect)
- Follow-ups: PR-19821 (streaming reconnect), PR-19827 (standardized overload responses + Retry-After in dataplane)
